_comment: Numbers the page renders. Upload a new copy of this file and the page
updates — no HTML change, no redeploy of anything else.
`decode` is a best recorded rate on that machine, or null for 'not
measured'. Null renders as 'not measured' rather than a blank or a zero,
because a missing measurement and a slow one are different claims.
`modes` is how the model runs there: gpu = fully resident, ssd = experts
stream from disk, hyb = split CPU/GPU. Several modes means the app can
use any of them; an empty list renders 'does not fit'.
_provenance: The M4 mini and DGX Spark rows were measured directly on those machines in August 2026 and carry the method in their notes. The M1 Ultra and M2 Max rows are still carried over verbatim from the first version of this page and have NOT been re-verified; replace them with exported measurements before treating them as current. Prices are approximate street or list prices in August 2026, recorded so a rate can be read against what the machine costs — they move, and they are not quotes.

boxes.label: M1 Ultra · 64-core GPU · 128 GB
boxes.price: from $3,999 at launch · discontinued, used market
boxes.note: Best decode recorded on this machine, each model on the engine the app picks for it — llama.cpp for the dense-ish Qwen, our own Rust/Metal engine for the four big MoEs. The last two rows are out-of-core rates: neither model fits 128 GB, so the weights stream from disk and the cost is visible in the number.

boxes.label: M2 Max · 64 GB
boxes.note: The same catalogue, scored for 64 GB. Laguna-S still fits in memory; DeepSeek-V4-Flash no longer does and moves out-of-core, which is what the 2.9 costs — the same file, a different machine, a different answer.

boxes.label: M4 mini · 16 GB
boxes.note: A 16 GB machine is offered the models that suit it, not the whole catalogue. Both rows were re-measured on this machine in August 2026, decode isolated as the difference between a 129-token and a 1-token completion so that prefill is excluded. The larger Qwen3 variants are absent because they cannot be tested here rather than because they are slow: 14B needs a download this machine has no room for, and 32B is a 20 GB file on a 16 GB machine with 12.7 GB free — it cannot be stored, let alone run.

boxes.label: DGX Spark · GB10 · 128 GB
boxes.note: Not a Local Mind machine — the app is macOS only. This is the same DeepSeek-V4-Flash file on an NVIDIA GB10 Grace Blackwell desktop through the reference CUDA engine, so the model and the quantisation are comparable to the Mac rows even though the engine is not. Measured August 2026 as an A/B/B/A sequence, three repetitions per arm, GPU clock sampled throughout (2405–2535 MHz); the repetitions spanned 0.06 tok/s. The weights sit in unified memory rather than streaming, which is why an 87 GB model reports a resident rate on a 128 GB box.
